papers.title: Inorganic Sol-Gel Polymerization for Hydrogel Bioprinting.
papers.abstract: An inorganic sol-gel polymerization process was used as a cross-linking reaction during three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting of cell-containing hydrogel scaffolds. Hybrid hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC), with a controlled ratio of silylation, was prepared and isolated as a 3D-network precursor. When dissolved in a biological buffer containing human mesenchymal stem cells, it yields a bioink that can be printed during polymerization by extrusion. It is worth noting that the sol-gel process proceeded at pH 7.4 using biocompatible mode of catalysis (NaF and glycine). The printing window was determined by rheology and viscosity measurements. The physicochemical properties of hydrogels were studied. Covalent functionalization of the network can be easily performed by adding a triethoxysilyl-containing molecule; a fluorescent hybrid molecule was used as a proof of concept.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及水凝胶生物打印的化学交联方法，但完全没有使用AI技术。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI or machine learning into any stage of the bioprinting workflow; it focuses solely on the chemical sol-gel polymerization process for hydrogel formation.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种生物相容的溶胶-凝胶交联方法用于水凝胶生物打印。
summary_zh.method: 通过硅烷化羟丙甲纤维素制备杂化水凝胶，并在生理pH下用氟化钠和甘氨酸催化溶胶-凝胶聚合。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印了含人间充质干细胞的水凝胶支架，并研究了其理化性质。
summary_zh.validation: 通过流变学和粘度测量确定打印窗口，并表征水凝胶性能。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a biocompatible cross-linking method for hydrogel bioprinting using inorganic sol-gel polymerization.
summary_en.method: Hybrid hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose with controlled silylation was prepared, dissolved in buffer with mesenchymal stem cells, and printed during sol-gel polymerization catalyzed by NaF and glycine at pH 7.4.
summary_en.result: Hydrogel scaffolds containing human mesenchymal stem cells were successfully printed, and their physicochemical properties were characterized.
summary_en.validation: The printing window was determined by rheology and viscosity measurements, and hydrogel properties were studied.

papers.title: Immersion Bioprinting of Tumor Organoids in Multi-Well Plates for Increasing Chemotherapy Screening Throughput.
papers.abstract: The current drug development pipeline takes approximately fifteen years and $2.6 billion to get a new drug to market. Typically, drugs are tested on two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures and animal models to estimate their efficacy before reaching human trials. However, these models are often not representative of the human body. The 2D culture changes the morphology and physiology of cells, and animal models often have a vastly different anatomy and physiology than humans. The use of bioengineered human cell-based organoids may increase the probability of success during human trials by providing human-specific preclinical data. They could also be deployed for personalized medicine diagnostics to optimize therapies in diseases such as cancer. However, one limitation in employing organoids in drug screening has been the difficulty in creating large numbers of homogeneous organoids in form factors compatible with high-throughput screening (e.g., 96- and 384-well plates). Bioprinting can be used to scale up deposition of such organoids and tissue constructs. Unfortunately, it has been challenging to 3D print hydrogel bioinks into small-sized wells due to well-bioink interactions that can result in bioinks spreading out and wetting the well surface instead of maintaining a spherical form. Here, we demonstrate an immersion printing technique to bioprint tissue organoids in 96-well plates to increase the throughput of 3D drug screening. A hydrogel bioink comprised of hyaluronic acid and collagen is bioprinted into a viscous gelatin bath, which blocks the bioink from interacting with the well walls and provides support to maintain a spherical form. This method was validated using several cancerous cell lines, and then applied to patient-derived glioblastoma (GBM) and sarcoma biospecimens for drug screening.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高肿瘤类器官药物筛选的通量。
summary_zh.method: 将水凝胶生物墨水浸入明胶浴中打印到多孔板中。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印多种癌细胞系和患者来源的类器官用于药筛。
summary_zh.validation: 使用癌细胞系和患者样本进行体外验证。

summary_en.motivation: To increase the throughput of drug screening by enabling bioprinting of homogeneous tumor organoids in multi-well plates.
summary_en.method: An immersion printing technique deposits hydrogel bioink into a gelatin support bath to maintain spherical organoid shape and prevent well-wall wetting.
summary_en.result: The method produced viable organoids from multiple cancer cell lines and patient-derived glioblastoma and sarcoma specimens for drug screening.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation using cancerous cell lines and patient-derived biospecimens demonstrated the utility for 3D drug screening.

papers.title: Nucleotide lipid-based hydrogel as a new biomaterial ink for biofabrication.
papers.abstract: One of the greatest challenges in the field of biofabrication remains the discovery of suitable bioinks that satisfy physicochemical and biological requirements. Despite recent advances in tissue engineering and biofabrication, progress has been limited to the development of technologies using polymer-based materials. Here, we show that a nucleotide lipid-based hydrogel resulting from the self-assembly of nucleotide lipids can be used as a bioink for soft tissue reconstruction using injection or extrusion-based systems. To the best of our knowledge, the use of a low molecular weight hydrogel as an alternative to polymeric bioinks is a novel concept in biofabrication and 3D bioprinting. Rheological studies revealed that nucleotide lipid-based hydrogels exhibit suitable mechanical properties for biofabrication and 3D bioprinting, including i) fast gelation kinetics in a cell culture medium and ii) shear moduli and thixotropy compatible with extruded oral cell survival (human gingival fibroblasts and stem cells from the apical papilla). This polymer-free soft material is a promising candidate for a new bioink design.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI or machine learning into any stage of the bioprinting workflow; it solely describes a new hydrogel material and its rheological properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适合软组织重建的新型生物墨水材料。
summary_zh.method: 利用核苷酸脂质自组装形成低分子量水凝胶作为生物墨水。
summary_zh.result: 该水凝胶具有快速凝胶动力学和适合细胞存活的剪切模量。
summary_zh.validation: 流变学研究和细胞存活实验验证了其适用性。

summary_en.motivation: To discover novel bioinks that satisfy both physicochemical and biological requirements for soft tissue reconstruction.
summary_en.method: A low molecular weight hydrogel formed by self-assembly of nucleotide lipids was used as a bioink for extrusion-based bioprinting.
summary_en.result: The hydrogel exhibited fast gelation in cell culture medium and shear moduli/thixotropy compatible with cell survival.
summary_en.validation: Rheological characterization and cell viability assays were performed.
